runConfig.positivePrompt: Scientific educational image-to-video for ages five to fourteen. Static locked wide camera, one continuous forward-only five-second shot with no cuts. Preserve the attached approved still as the exact first-frame Ankylosaurus magniventris identity, low broad full-body anatomy, left-facing composition, wetland, lighting, palette, armor pattern, ground, and crop reference. Exactly one complete Ankylosaurus remains with one broad flat skull, small beaked mouth, two connected neck half-rings, irregular low osteoderms, exactly four planted legs, one complete continuous tail, and one integrated low oval tail club. After a brief low-browse hold, the dinosaur itself raises the complete skull, throat, connected neck half-rings, shoulder base, and upper chest together by a clearly visible seven to nine degrees in one smooth direction. The beak stays closed. The final second holds the new higher attentive pose. Keep the broad torso, pelvis, armor rows, all four feet, every readable toe, complete tail, and single club stable at their source coordinates. Keep all water, plants, clouds, trees, shadows, and ground completely still. No return, reverse, second nod, chew, step, tail swing, body turn, or loop.
